title: Derived Chow etale neighbourhood with a pseudo-coherent kernel
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pullback and tensor use K-flat resolutions; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Pseudo-coherent means etale locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and of finite presentation, and let $x\in|X|$. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, a finitely presented closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow T=X\times_A P$, where $P=\mathbf P^n_A$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], a point $z\in|Z|$, an open subscheme $V\subset P$, and $E\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ with the following properties. Put $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to P$, $b=p\circ h$, $c=q\circ h$, and $W=c^{-1}(V)$. The restriction $j=c|_W:W\hookrightarrow V$ is a finitely presented closed immersion (so $W$ is a scheme), $b|_W:W\to X$ is etale, $z\in W$ and $b(z)=x$. The object $E$ is pseudo-coherent and all its cohomology sheaves vanish off $h(Z)$, and there is an isomorphism $E|_{X\times_A V}\simeq(h_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]|_{X\times_A V}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{X\times_A V})$.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, clauses (1)--(5); finite presentation of j as noted in Tag 0CTS, lemma-compute-Fourier-Mukai-for-derived-chow.

proof.text: Order the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A_0\subset A$ by inclusion. The inverse-limit presentation [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], followed by the essential-surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category], gives a finitely presented algebraic space $X_0/A_0$ whose pullback is $X$. After enlarging $A_0$, [lem-sfb-space-descend-separated] makes $X_0/A_0$ separated. Let $x_0$ be the image of $x$. The scheme $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to its finite-type map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. We first construct the required data over $S_0$, then pull them back; the last steps verify every assertion under this arbitrary base change.

The space $X_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. Choose a surjective affine etale chart $U_0\to X_0$ using [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], and choose $u_0\in U_0$ above $x_0$. Since finite presentation is tested on etale scheme charts, $U_0\to S_0$ is locally of finite presentation; between affine schemes this is finite type. Thus [lem-chow-affine-immersion] gives an immersion $e:U_0\to P_0=\mathbf P^n_{A_0}$ through a closed immersion into its standard affine chart. Let $Y_0\hookrightarrow P_0$ be the scheme-theoretic image, which exists by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. The scheme $P_0$ is proper over $S_0$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and quasi-separated. The immersion $e$ is quasi-compact: $U_0$ is affine and $P_0$ is quasi-separated, so [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applies. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], identify $U_0$ with a quasi-compact open subscheme $O_0\subset Y_0$. Choose an open $V_0\subset P_0$ with $V_0\cap Y_0=O_0$; this is precisely the subspace-topology characterization of an open in the closed subscheme $Y_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, second paragraph: affine chart and its projective closure.

proof.text: The projection $X_0\times_{S_0}Y_0\to Y_0$ is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $X_0/S_0$ (on a scheme test this just pulls back the defining ideal). The pair consisting of $U_0\to X_0$ and $U_0=O_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ is a section over $O_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-partial-section-schematic-image] to obtain its smallest closed image $Z_0\subset X_0\times_{S_0}Y_0$, isomorphic to $O_0$ over $O_0$. Compose its closed inclusion with $X_0\times Y_0\hookrightarrow T_0=X_0\times P_0$ to obtain $h_0$. These are closed immersions on every scheme test: base change pulls back ideals and composition is the quotient by the inverse-image ideal. Consequently $W_0=c_0^{-1}(V_0)\simeq O_0\simeq U_0$, $j_0:W_0\to V_0$ is the closed immersion $Y_0\cap V_0\hookrightarrow V_0$, and $b_0|_{W_0}$ is the chosen etale chart. The image of $u_0$ is a point of $W_0$ above $x_0$. The same smallest-image property also makes $Z_0$ the schematic closure of this graph in $T_0$, since any closed subspace of $T_0$ containing the graph intersects $X_0\times Y_0$ in a closed subspace containing it.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, second paragraph, application of 0CP3.

proof.text: The scheme $P_0$ has a finite standard affine cover by polynomial algebras over $A_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]; its charts are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The space $T_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], since $X_0,P_0,S_0$ are so. The base changes of the chart $U_0\to X_0$ to these projective charts are etale charts of $T_0$ represented by affine schemes of finite type over $A_0$, hence Noetherian by the same scheme theorem. Thus $T_0$ is Noetherian in the etale-chart sense. Both closed subspaces $Z_0\subset T_0$ and $Y_0\subset P_0$ are Noetherian by [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules]; $P_0$ is Noetherian, being covered by finitely many Noetherian affine charts and separated over the affine $S_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, second and third paragraphs: Noetherian ambient spaces.

proof.text: The structure sheaf of a Noetherian space is coherent (on affine etale charts it is a Noetherian ring). By [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules], $F_0=h_{0,*}\mathcal O_{Z_0}$ is coherent with support $h_0(Z_0)$. Take $E_0=F_0[0]$; restriction gives $E_0|_{X_0\times V_0}=h_{0,*}\mathcal O_{Z_0}[0]|_{X_0\times V_0}$ literally. Pseudo-coherence in the sense of [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex]: for an object $V\to T_0$ of the small etale model, the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the schemes $V\times_{T_0}U_k$, with $U_k$ the finite-type affine charts of step 4, generate a covering sieve; each $R$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring of $U_k$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. On such a chart, [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] (equivalence, cohomology comparison, faithfulness) gives $F_0|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\simeq a_R(N)$ with $N=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,F_0)$, finitely generated by coherence on this etale chart. As $R$ is Noetherian, successive surjections $R^{r_0}\to N$, $R^{r_1}\to\ker$, ... give a resolution $L^\bullet\to N$ by finite free modules, $L^n=0$ for $n>0$. Exactness of $a_R$ makes $a_R(L^\bullet)\to F_0|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ a quasi-isomorphism with terms $a_R(R^{r})=\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$. So $E_0$ is pseudo-coherent. Coherent modules are finitely presented, so [lem-sfb-space-closed-structure-finite-presentation] makes $h_0$ and $Y_0\hookrightarrow P_0$ (closed in the Noetherian $P_0$) finitely presented closed immersions; the ideal of $j_0:W_0=Y_0\cap V_0\hookrightarrow V_0$ is the restriction of that of $Y_0$, still of finite type, so the same theorem makes $j_0$ finitely presented. This verifies all required properties over $A_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, third paragraph (08IK); finite presentation as in Tag 0CTS.

proof.text: Pull $P_0,V_0,Z_0$ back from $A_0$ to $A$ and retain the same integer $n$. Projective base change identifies $P_0\times_{A_0}A$ with $P=\mathbf P^n_A$ [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. The closed immersions $h_0,j_0$ pull back to closed immersions $h,j$; their finite presentation persists because, on any affine scheme test, a finite generating list for the defining ideal pulls back to a generating list for the inverse-image ideal, and closed immersions are affine and quasi-separated. Associativity of fibre products gives $W=c^{-1}(V)=W_0\times_{X_0}X$. The map $W\to X$ is etale: it is representable, and on every scheme test it is a scheme base change of the etale chart $W_0\to X_0$; apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. To choose $z$, apply [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] with $E=X_0$, $C=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ and $U=W_0$, to the point $x$ and the point corresponding to $u_0$. It supplies a point of $W_0\times_{X_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, hence a point $z\in W$ above $x$. Existence, rather than uniqueness, is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, first paragraph, pullback of geometric data (correcting the uniqueness slip).

proof.text: Write $a_T:T\to T_0$ and define $E=La_T^*E_0$ using [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback]. The local finite-free characterization [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex] represents $E_0$ etale locally by a bounded-above finite free complex. Such a complex is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Termwise tensor pullback therefore computes $E$ there and remains bounded-above finite free, proving pseudo-coherence. For support, the complement of $h(Z)$ is the inverse image of the complement of $h_0(Z_0)$: on scheme tests this is the equality $V(I\mathcal O_T)=a_T^{-1}V(I)$. On this open $E_0$ restricts to zero, so its derived pullback is zero. Restriction and pullback compose by the specified comparisons of [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback]. Thus every cohomology sheaf of $E$ vanishes off $h(Z)$.

source.place: Tag 0CTR, lemma-derived-chow, first paragraph; pseudo-coherent pullback as in 08H4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-flat-closed-kernel-base-change] with $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y_0=V_0$, and the closed immersion $i_0:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{A_0}V_0$. Its relative flatness assumption holds because $W_0\to X_0$ is etale and etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], tested on charts. The map $V_0\to S_0$ is flat: standard projective charts are polynomial algebras [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], whose projections are flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]; restricting further to opens preserves flatness on local rings. Writing $a_V:X\times V\to X_0\times V_0$ for the restricted projection, the comparison gives $La_V^*(i_{0,*}\mathcal O_{W_0}[0])\simeq i_*\mathcal O_W[0]$. Restriction and derived composition [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback] identify the left object with $E|_{X\times V}$. Ordinary direct image restricted to a target open is direct image of the restriction, as is seen from the defining chart limits [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; hence $i_*\mathcal O_W[0]=(h_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]|_{X\times V}$. This proves the asserted derived isomorphism on the whole open $X\times_A V$ and completes the construction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q45-b4099ace3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: Stacks 0CTR with its whole proof, 0CTS first paragraph, 0CTQ with footnote (spaces-more-morphisms.tex), 0CP3 (spaces-morphisms.tex) and 08IR (spaces-perfect.tex), plus the item, both new nodes and all 28 cited statements. The statement matches 0CTR (1)-(5). The finite presentation of j is proved in 0CTS, so nothing is weakened. Confirmed source error: 0CTR says 'the unique point' mapping to x, but A'=F_3, A=F_9, W'=Spec F_9 gives two points over x. The worker's step 6 uses only existence, via lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point. Both new nodes are true, statement-only tools and not duplicates. The partial-section node is the space form of 0CP3; the existing nagata node covers schemes only, and X_0×Y_0 is a space. The kernel node is the space form of the scheme node 0CTA, built from 0CTQ+08IR, and is needed because X_0 is a space. Fault C4/E6 in step 5: pseudo-coherence was taken from lem-sfb-space-noetherian-pseudocoherent-criterion, whose statement uses the m-wise strictly-perfect notion. The item and step 7 use def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex, a local bounded-above finite-free model, and no cited node bridges the two. Step 4/5 also used, without a node, that the open V_0 of P_0 is Noetherian. FIX: step 5 now proves the def-sfb notion directly. It uses Noetherian affine charts Spec R of V×_{T_0}U_k, lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization to get F_0≅a_R(N) with N finite, and a finite free resolution with exactness of a_R. j_0 is finitely presented as the restriction of the finite-type ideal of Y_0⊂P_0. The step-4 sentence was adjusted. In proof_deps the criterion is replaced by the realization node, which is in the same unit and already in the dropped criterion's closure, so no cycle appears. Batch-5: the trf citations are definitions and foundations (def-trf-algebraic-space, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers), not steps of the trace-formula or Poincaré proofs, so they are accepted. lean.statement: theorem exists_derivedChow_neighbourhood (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec A)) [∀ Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec A), HasDerivedCategory.{w} Y.SmallModules] (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ a ↦ IsClosedImmersion a.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (hlfp : ∀ (U : Over (Spec A)) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFinitePresentation U.hom) (x : Point X.obj.obj) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (T Z Tᵥ : AlgebraicSpace (Spec A)) (p : T ⟶ X) (q : T ⟶ schemeSpace (chowProjectiveSpace A n)) (h : Z ⟶ T) (V : (chowProjectiveSpace A n).left.Opens) (r : Tᵥ ⟶ T) (qᵥ : Tᵥ ⟶ schemeSpace (chowProjectiveOpen A n V)) (W : Over (Spec A)) (k : schemeSpace W ⟶ Z) (j : W ⟶ chowProjectiveOpen A n V) (z : Point Z.obj.obj) (w₀ : W.left) (E : T.DerivedModules), Nonempty (IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk p.hom.hom q.hom.hom)) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ a ↦ IsClosedImmersion a.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation a.left) h.hom.hom ∧ IsPullback r.hom.hom qᵥ.hom.hom q.hom.hom (chowProjectiveOpenInclusion A n V).hom.hom ∧ IsPullback k.hom.hom (yoneda.map j) (h ≫ q).hom.hom (chowProjectiveOpenInclusion A n V).hom.hom ∧ IsClosedImmersion j.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.left ∧ IsEtale (k ≫ h ≫ p).hom.hom ∧ schemePointMap k.hom.hom w₀ = z ∧ mapPoint (h ≫ p).hom.hom z = x ∧ T.IsPseudoCoherent E ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, moduleSupport ((T.smallModuleEquivalence.inverse).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor T.SmallModules i).obj E)) ⊆ pointImage h.hom.hom) ∧ Nonempty ((spaceDerivedPullback r).obj E ≅ (spaceDerivedPullback r).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor T.SmallModules 0).obj ((smallModuleDirectImage h).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.smallStructureRings))))
